newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT- Coffee poised to extend gains.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- Coffee poised to extend gains.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Further rises are awaited in coffee prices when London opens on Wednesday, analysts said.
"It's due $60 up on figures, but we're looking for something more like $10-15," one London trader said.

Traders in Asia were looking for much bigger rises. They tipped London robusta futures to rise by $50-200 on the back of a blistering rally in New York, although they said the market may soon be in for a correction.
"The market is jumping all over the place. I think it may move up some more. London is due $60 higher," a senior coffee dealer for a commodity firm in Singapore told Reuters.
"There's a chance it could move up further. It's been building support," Susan Rigg, a technical analyst at Chart Analysis, said.
It would take a move down through $1,700 to negate the uptrend, Rigg said.
The July robusta contract in London touched a new high of $1,835 a tonne on Tuesday, the highest since May 1996, before closing $40 up on the day at $1,815.

In New York, the July contract soared to a lifetime high of 243.00 U.S. cents/lb before settling on Tuesday 11.50 cents up on the day at 241.15. The contract rose 11.75 cents on Monday, giving a total of 23.25 cents/lb so far this week.
Traders said uncertainty over Colombia's ability to meet export commitments because of tight supplies, and the approach of the frost season in Brazil would also provide a boost to coffee prices.
